literal: To the ear food not having time, a little to the stomach also will be given.
translation: When there is no food for the ear, a little may be given to the stomach as well.
modern: செவிக்கு அறிவாகிய உணவு கிடைக்காத போது, உடலை வளர்க்கும் வயிற்றுக்கும் சிறிது உணவு தரப்படும்.
explanation: This couplet contrasts the nourishment of the mind with the nourishment of the body. The phrase 'food for the ear' refers to learning and listening to wisdom, which is presented as the primary human need. Only when there is no opportunity to feed the ear should one provide a little food to the stomach. The suffix 'um' (also/even) attached to the stomach emphasizes that physical hunger is strictly secondary to intellectual growth.
